key: He judged the cause of the poor and needy; Then it was well. Is not this to know Me? saith the LORD.
s: Rebuking a king who builds by unpaid labour, the prophet holds up his father, who did justice; Metzudat David, on 22:16, takes such judging as knowing God because by it he cleaves to God’s own deeds, pitying the poor as God does.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, Jeremiah 22:16, at [421,16]). Plain sense faithful: 22:13 to 14 the woe on him who builds his house using his neighbour’s service without wages (Jehoiakim, named at 22:18, as Rashi, Radak and Metzudat David on 22:13 all say), 22:15 the father who did justice and righteousness; no four-word repeat of the key. Metzudat David on 22:16 says judging the poor is knowing God because by it he cleaves to God’s deeds, having compassion on the poor as God does; the reading paraphrases exactly that. Rashi has nothing on 22:16 and Radak only cross-refers, so Metzudat David is the right choice. Entry passes entry-check.
